title: Design System: Dong Que Quan München

display.purpose: The two-line hero identity and its red poster strip.

headline.purpose: Uppercase section headlines and oversized service statements.

title.purpose: Dish cards, menu groups, speciality names, and local titles.

body.purpose: Descriptions, addresses, instructions, and narrative copy.

label.purpose: Navigation, filters, prices, metadata, and compact controls.

shadows.name: offset-photograph
shadows.purpose: Depth under the offset interior photograph only.

shadows.name: floating-utility
shadows.purpose: Cart launcher and toast feedback only.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Shared tactile easing for controls, media, and entry states.

motion.name: control-standard
motion.purpose: Button, border, filter, and color transitions.

motion.name: hero-copy-enter
motion.purpose: One-time rise and deblur for the hero copy sequence.

motion.name: hero-image-settle
motion.purpose: One-time scale and color settle for the first-view food image.

motion.name: cart-enter
motion.purpose: Side-panel entrance when motion is allowed.

motion.name: repeated-reveal
motion.purpose: Generic section reveal classes are intentionally neutralized in the redesign.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The decisive action for menu discovery, reservation, form submission, and recovery states.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:50px; padding:.84rem 1.35rem; border:0; border-radius:var(--radius-sm,10px); background:var(--signal,#c03743); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); font:700 .82rem/1.1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background .25s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)),transform .2s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:var(--signal-dark,#9f2833); transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:scale(.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--herb,#87b99a); outline-offset:4px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-btn-primary { transition-duration:.01ms; } }

components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:50px; padding:.84rem 1.35rem; border:1px solid var(--night-line-strong,rgba(243,239,228,.34)); border-radius:var(--radius-sm,10px); background:rgba(16,20,18,.48); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); font:700 .82rem/1.1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background .25s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)),border-color .25s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)),color .25s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)),transform .2s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); background:var(--paper,#f3efe4); color:var(--ink,#101412); transform:translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform:scale(.98); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--herb,#87b99a); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Menu Filter
components.description: A compact, scrollable category filter; the active state uses the primary red fill.
components.css: .ds-filter-strip { display:flex; gap:.5rem; overflow-x:auto; padding:.2rem 0 .35rem; scrollbar-width:none; } .ds-filter-strip::-webkit-scrollbar { display:none; } .ds-filter { flex:0 0 auto; min-height:42px; padding:.52rem .9rem; border:1px solid var(--night-line,rgba(243,239,228,.16)); border-radius:var(--radius-sm,10px); background:transparent; color:var(--paper-muted,#c7c6b9); font:700 .78rem/1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background .2s,border-color .2s,color .2s; } .ds-filter:hover { border-color:var(--paper-muted,#c7c6b9); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); } .ds-filter.is-active { border-color:var(--signal,#c03743); background:var(--signal,#c03743); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); } .ds-filter:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--herb,#87b99a); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Menu Search Field
components.description: The compact full-text field paired with the sticky menu filter strip.
components.css: .ds-field { display:grid; gap:.45rem; color:var(--paper-muted,#c7c6b9); font:700 .75rem/1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; letter-spacing:.05em; } .ds-field input { width:100%; min-height:48px; padding:.75rem .9rem; border:1px solid var(--night-line,rgba(243,239,228,.16)); border-radius:var(--radius-sm,10px); background:var(--ink,#101412); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); caret-color:var(--signal,#c03743); font:400 1rem/1.65 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; transition:border-color .2s var(--ease,cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-field input::placeholder { color:#8e958d; } .ds-field input:focus { border-color:var(--herb,#87b99a); outline:3px solid var(--herb,#87b99a); outline-offset:4px; }

components.css: .ds-menu-item { display:grid; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) auto; column-gap:1.5rem; min-height:11rem; padding:1.45rem 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--night-line,rgba(243,239,228,.16)); color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); } .ds-menu-head { display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:.75rem; } .ds-menu-head span { color:var(--signal-bright,#df747c); font:700 .76rem/1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; letter-spacing:.06em; } .ds-menu-head h3 { margin:0; color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); font:700 1rem/1.2 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; letter-spacing:-.02em; } .ds-menu-item>strong { font:700 1rem/1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; white-space:nowrap; } .ds-menu-item>p,.ds-menu-item>small { grid-column:1; margin-left:3rem; } .ds-menu-item>p { margin-top:.45rem; margin-bottom:0; color:var(--paper-muted,#c7c6b9); font:400 .88rem/1.6 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-menu-item>small { margin-top:.35rem; color:var(--muted,#9aa299); font:600 .75rem/1.4 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; letter-spacing:.04em; } .ds-menu-item>button { grid-column:2; align-self:end; min-height:36px; padding:.42rem .75rem; border:1px solid var(--night-line-strong,rgba(243,239,228,.34)); border-radius:0; background:transparent; color:var(--paper,#f3efe4); font:700 .76rem/1 Manrope,Arial,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-menu-item>button:hover { border-color:var(--signal-bright,#df747c); color:var(--signal-bright,#df747c); } .ds-menu-item>button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--herb,#87b99a); outline-offset:4px; }

narrative.overview:
The interface feels like a contemporary Vietnamese night-market poster printed on a dark matchbook: near-black stock, warm paper ink, lacquer-red blocks, tightly packed sans-serif type, and real food photography. It is energetic without becoming noisy, premium without becoming delicate, and unmistakably restaurant-first.

The system replaces the former luminous porcelain and serif world. Manrope carries every role, from oversized headlines to operating details. Hierarchy comes from scale, compression, color blocks, asymmetric image mosaics, and tonal layers rather than ornamental typography or generic pan-Asian motifs.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black page stock with slightly raised dark-green surfaces.
Tight, uppercase Manrope headlines and plain-spoken Manrope body copy.
Lacquer red for decisive actions and poster fields; brighter red for small labels on dark.
Warm paper text instead of pure white; herb green only for vegetarian meaning and keyboard focus.
Asymmetric food and interior mosaics with one consistent 14px crop radius.
One opening hero-settle sequence; repeated section reveals are intentionally disabled.

rules.name: The Red Block Rule
rules.body: Lacquer red may become a large field only when the surface reads as a deliberate poster, such as the hero title strip or lunch section; elsewhere it marks action and selection.

rules.name: The Herb Means Something Rule
rules.body: Herb green is not decoration. Reserve it for vegetarian meaning and focus visibility.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: Use Manrope throughout; do not reintroduce the retired serif as a display flourish.

rules.name: The Poster Compression Rule
rules.body: H1–h3 stay uppercase, heavy, tightly tracked, and closely led. Body copy remains sentence case and breathable.

rules.name: The Ledger Holds Still Rule
rules.body: Filtering and searching may change menu content, but toolbar position, stable price alignment, and the visitor’s reading anchor must remain calm.

rules.name: The Flat Poster Rule
rules.body: Do not add shadows to food cards, menu rows, forms, or poster sections; use tone, crop, hairlines, and overlap first.

rules.name: The Ten-and-Fourteen Rule
rules.body: Use 10px for touch controls and 14px for media or surfaces; avoid pills and avoid inventing extra radius tiers.

dos: Do use real, dish-specific photography as the richest color in the interface.
Do keep headline composition blocky, uppercase, and tightly compressed.
Do reserve large Lacquer Red fields for the hero title strip and lunch poster.
Do keep the long menu searchable, filterable, horizontally scrollable on mobile, and visually aligned like a ledger.
Do preserve the one-time hero settle, tactile state feedback, reduced-motion behavior, and the 820px one-column transition.
Do use 10px controls and 14px media or surfaces consistently.
donts: Don't restore the porcelain background, serif display typography, gold ornament, or capsule-control language from the previous world.
Don't use Herb as a general accent or Signal Red for large fills.
Don't add generic repeated scroll reveals, parallax, or decorative motion after the opening hero sequence.
Don't add shadows to ordinary cards or ledger rows.
Don't introduce generic pan-Asian motifs, sushi-coded decoration, or fabricated heritage cues.
Don't reuse one food image to represent a different named dish.
